In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Asian countries have made great strides in the last two decades in developing their industrial capabilities.
the Asian economies have been successful in their export drive and have been able to improve their competitiveness, and that the policy measures have contributed to this.
the Asian countries, in the aggregate, have done well in terms of competitiveness and are likely to continue to do well in the future, provided they maintain their present course of action.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
competitiveness is not just a matter of the right policy framework but that it also depends on the quality of the firms in an economy and their ability to compete internationally.
the Asian experience is one in which a combination of policy and institutional reform, and the creation of a supportive business environment, has been a key factor in the region's success.

competitiveness is not just a matter of the market, but also the state, that it is not just about the firm, but also about the national system of innovation, and that it is not simply the product of a few key factors, but the result of a complex set of interrelated factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
competitiveness is the result of a combination of firm-level and national factors.
the competitiveness of a country is determined by the quality of its firms, and the quality of its people.
there is a strong correlation between the competitiveness of a nation's economy and the level of technological development of its enterprises.
